item.title: ASET, RSET and DIFF maps
item.description:
This page reads tracked FDS output. You do not need to run FDS.

The ASET-RSET comparison asks whether people can leave before conditions turn untenable. Schröder, Arnold and Seyfried (2020) turned it from one number into maps over the floor. pyfds_evac.analysis builds those maps from a finished run and from FDS output:

  • the ASET map is, for each map cell, the first time the fire makes it untenable;
  • the RSET map is, for each cell, the last time anyone is in it;
  • DIFF = ASET − RSET. Negative means the fire wins in that cell.

The module post-processes: it changes no simulation. It needs pedpy>=1.5.1 for the RSET map, which pyFDS-Evac now requires.

A runnable example

The script is examples/aset_rset_maps.py. Run it from the repository root (runtime about 10 s):

uv run python examples/aset_rset_maps.py

It takes the 10 × 10 m gas room of assets/iso_table22_coupled (deck e) and 20 people leaving through the corner exit in clear air. The gas of that deck is uniform, so its ASET map is flat and only the RSET map varies; a real study uses a fire that varies in space. The FED limit is 0.05 here so that the room fails somewhere.

ASET from the FDS output

read_crossings returns, for every node of the slices, the first time each criterion is met, and the height of the slice it read.

criteria = AsetCriteria(
 visibility_limit_m=None, temperature_c=None, heat_fed=None, fed=0.05
)
crossings = read_crossings(FDS, criteria)
for crossing in crossings:
 print(
 f"{crossing.name}: slice at z = {crossing.z_m} m, data to {crossing.horizon_s:.0f} s"
 )

RSET from the runs

One run per seed. Passing exit_times lets the map tell an agent that left from one still inside when the run ended.

scenario = load_scenario("assets/iso_table22_coupled/config_a.json")
spawn = scenario.distributions["jps-distributions_0"]
spawn["coordinates"] = [[1, 1], [1, 5], [5, 5], [5, 1], [1, 1]]
spawn["parameters"].update(number=20, use_premovement=False)

rsets, grid = [], None
for seed in SEEDS:
 result = run_scenario(scenario, seed=seed)
 trajectory, walkable = load_trajectory(result.sqlite_file)
 grid = grid or grid_from_walkable(walkable, CELL)
 rsets.append(rset_map(trajectory, walkable, grid, exit_times=result.exit_times))
 print(
 f"seed {seed}: {len(result.exit_times)} left, remaining {result.agents_remaining}"
 )
 result.cleanup()
assert grid is not None

DIFF, per seed and pooled 

aset = aset_map(grid, crossings)
per_seed = [measures(diff_map(aset, rset, grid)) for rset in rsets]
for name, interval in seed_measures(per_seed).items():
 print(
 f"{name}: mean {interval.mean:.2f}, 95 % CI {interval.low:.2f} to {interval.high:.2f}"
 )

pooled, pooled_values = pool_rset(rsets, "p95")
diff = diff_map(aset, pooled, grid)
m = measures(diff)
print(
 f"ASET {np.nanmin(aset.time_s):.0f} s everywhere on {int(grid.area.astype(bool).sum())} cells"
)
print(
 f"pooled RSET ({pooled_values.label}): last cell empty at {np.nanmax(pooled.time_s):.1f} s"
)
print(
 f"min DIFF {m.min_diff_s:.1f} s, failing area {m.fail_area_m2:.2f} m2, C {m.c_m2s:.1f} m2 s"
)
print(f"cells by state: { {k: v for k, v in m.counts.items() if v} }")

The printed lines on this commit include:

FED 0.05: slice at z = 1.5 m, data to 250 s
ASET 10 s everywhere on 289 cells
min DIFF -2.9 s, failing area 6.48 m2, C -9.7 m2 s
cells by state: {'pass': 97, 'fail': 18, 'aset_only': 174}

The script writes the figure to a new temporary directory and prints its path. To write it elsewhere, pass the path.

ASET, pooled RSET (95th percentile over n = 3 seeds) and DIFF = ASET − RSET, all in seconds, on 0.6 m cells, 20 people, clear air, FED limit 0.05, deck e of assets/iso_table22_coupled, drawn by plot_maps. Failing cells are hatched; cells nobody visited are grey; cells without a map are white. The FED map is for a person standing still from t = 0 at 1.5 m; it is not the dose of a walk. Regenerated by uv run python examples/aset_rset_maps.py site/static/images/analysis/aset_rset_diff.png.

The ASET criteria

A cell is untenable when any sample point in it meets a limit (the block maximum, as the study chose). A point on a cell edge belongs to both cells. AsetCriteria sets the limits; a None leaves a criterion out. The combined ASET is the earliest crossing of any selected criterion, and every criterion’s own map is kept in AsetMap.per_criterion, under the name of its crossing: K 0.3 (the K limit), T 45, FED 0.3 and heat FED 0.3, with the limits you set. AsetMap.deciding() names, per cell, the criterion that sets the ASET; criteria that tie are joined with + (K 0.3+T 45), and cells without data or never untenable are empty. plot_maps draws it as a fourth panel.

Criterion Per-point condition Default Source
Visibility extinction coefficient K ≥ C / Vlim Vlim = 10 m, C = 3, so K ≥ 0.3 1/m 10 m: Engineers Australia (2014) p. 15, NZBC C/VM2 p. 30, vfdb TB 04-01 Table 8.3. C: Jin, as quoted in vfdb p. 314 and ISO 13571 Note 2
Temperature T ≥ Tlim 45 °C, stay under 30 min; 50 °C for about 15 min and under 5 min (AsetCriteria.with_stay) vfdb TB 04-01 Table 8.3, DIN 18009-2 Table 1; dry air
Radiant flux (reference only) q ≥ qlim 1.7 kW/m² for a stay under 30 min, 2.0 for about 15 min, below 2.5 for under 5 min (vfdb); not computed by the module vfdb TB 04-01 Table 8.3, as listed in the criteria comparison. 1.7 is the no-pain critical flux of Wieczorek and Dembsey (2001), p. 96; ISO 13571:2012 §8.2 uses 2.5, where their Eq. (4) gives pain in about 22 s
Toxic FED FED of a person standing still from t = 0 ≥ 0.3 0.3, configurable ISO 13571 design criterion; the engine’s own rate functions
Heat FED convective heat FED, same person, ≥ 0.3 0.3, clothed law ISO 13571:2012 Eq. 9
  • Visibility and the limit are separate inputs. Schröder et al. use K ≥ 0.23 1/m (extinction_per_m=0.23, from the vfdb smoke density limit of 0.1 1/m) and 45 °C; the reproduction passes those.
  • Level criteria that AsetCriteria does not name (CO or HCl in ppm, CO₂ in per cent, a second extinction limit) come from read_level_crossing(fds_dir, quantity, limit, scale=...), with the FDS slice quantity name and scale from the volume fraction to the limit’s unit. It returns the same per-point crossing and feeds aset_map like the others.
  • The study uses no FED criterion. The FED and heat FED maps go beyond the paper.
  • The FED and heat FED maps are location-only: the dose of someone who stands at that point from t = 0, at the sampling height. It is not the dose of anyone’s walk, which is what the per-agent summary of the ASET check with FED gives.
  • Dose criteria are integrated per sample point, with the engine’s rule and clock (right endpoint, FED(t₀) = 0, one-second step, nearest slice frame), and the earliest point of a cell wins. A block-maximum concentration is never integrated.
  • The slices are read at the engine’s sampling height, 1.6 m by default; each result records the height of the slice it read.
  • A cell that never meets a limit by the end of the fire data is open, not filled with the last time. A criterion with shorter data cuts the others at its horizon.
  • A cell with no sample point or no floor has no data (NaN); it is never treated as safe.

The temperature limit assumes dry air, below 10 % water vapour by volume. The maps do not read humidity.

The RSET map and the five cell states

rset_map wraps PedPy’s compute_rset_map with the maximum per cell. The grid comes from PedPy’s own output, row 0 at the largest y, so ASET and RSET subtract with no flip; tests/test_analysis_rset.py fails if a PedPy release changes its grid.

A cell’s RSET is censored when it holds the last position of an agent that never left (a time limit, a deadlock, an incapacitated agent). Pass the run’s exit_times; without them the cells of the last frame are censored and a warning says so. From Python they are ScenarioResult.exit_times. A CLI run keeps them in an agent_exits table of its --output-sqlite file; load_exit_times(sqlite_file) reads it, and refuses a file without the table rather than guessing exits from the last frame.

State ASET RSET DIFF
pass exact exact ≥ 0
fail exact exact < 0
≥ bound open (not by the end of the fire data) exact > TF − RSET
≤ bound exact censored < ASET − TR
undetermined open censored none

Cells with an ASET but nobody walked there cannot fail; cells with an RSET but no ASET are a data gap. Both are counted and never passed.

Measures, seeds

measures gives, on the cells where DIFF is exact: the minimum DIFF and its cell, the failing area in m² (true floor area per cell), and C, the sum of DIFF times area over the failing cells in m² s, without binning. The paper’s C bins DIFF into 20 s classes; Measures.c_binned_m2s and release_measures give that only to compare with the paper. support is "intersection" (cells with both maps) or "union"; the failing area and C are the same, the shares and the coverage report differ.

One run per seed gives one RSET map. pool_rset takes the 95th percentile per cell over the seeds that visit it, and a cell censored in any seed stays censored. seed_measures gives each measure per seed with a 95 % bootstrap interval of the mean, and convergence_curve the interval half-width against the number of seeds. Choose the number of seeds from the curve. A maximum over seeds grows with their number; pool_seeds(..., "max") carries it as "max over n=…".

Sign visibility is a different map

Whether the signs of a route can be read through the smoke is a wayfinding question. It is not a tenability limit and is not part of DIFF. fdsvismap computes it separately (#140).

Verification against the data release

Run with SCHROEDER2020_RELEASE set to the unpacked Zenodo release (tests/test_analysis_zenodo.py; the release is not in the repository).

  • Stage 1, exact. The released difference map, counted by the release’s rules: min DIFF −29 s, 54 cells (19.44 m²) with DIFF ≤ 0, C = −310 m² s binned. By the default rules (DIFF = 0 passes, bin-free C): 52 cells, C = −274.7 m² s.
  • Stage 2, rebuild. ASET and RSET rebuilt with this module (PedPy RSET) against row A of scripts/docs/schroeder2020_reproduce.py: min DIFF differs by 2 s with the nearest and with the default exists cell rule; the failing cell count by −9 % (nearest) and −6 % (exists), all within the predeclared 10 s and 10 %. Row A reads the nearest node at the release’s grid points, so this checks the rebuild, not the release’s own cell rule.

Limits

  • The FED and heat FED maps are for a person standing still from t = 0; they are conservative and not a walker’s dose.
  • ASET is read on one slice height. The cell rules exists, all and nearest are available (cell_rule); the cell-centre rule of the study script is not.
  • The ASET is as fine as the slice output interval for the level criteria (visibility, temperature), and one second for the dose criteria.
  • RSET here is travel and modelled pre-movement from ignition. Detection and alarm times are not included (ISO/TR 16738).
  • With few seeds the 95th percentile lies near the maximum.
  • Research software. No result is a design or safety verdict.

References

  • Schröder, B., Arnold, L., Seyfried, A. (2020). A map representation of the ASET-RSET concept. Fire Safety Journal 115, 103154. doi:10.1016/j.firesaf.2020.103154
  • ISO 13571:2012, Life-threatening components of fire.
  • vfdb TB 04-01 (2020); DIN 18009-2:2021-06; Engineers Australia (2014), Practice Note for Tenability Criteria; MBIE C/VM2 Commentary.

See also ASET-RSET maps after Schröder et al. (2020) for the study these maps follow, and RSET from an ensemble of seeds.

item.title: How do I get the egress time and its spread from an ensemble of seeds?
item.description:
This how-to reads tracked FDS output. You do not need to run FDS. Part 1 needs no FDS output at all.

↓ Download the files for this page (22 kB zip)

Run the scenario once per seed. Read each agent’s exit time from the trajectory file, not from result.evacuation_time. Then report the last exit time over the seeds as a mean, a standard deviation (SD), a range and a high percentile, not as a single value.

What the simulation gives you

ISO/TR 16738 splits the required safe escape time as

RSET = tdet + ta + tpre + ttrav

where tdet is the detection time, ta the alarm time, tpre the pre-movement time and ttrav the travel time, all in seconds.

A pyFDS-Evac run starts at t = 0 and gives at most tpre + ttrav. It includes tpre only if the scenario models pre-movement (use_premovement in a spawn area; a spawn area that sets no pre-movement key gets a constant 10 s, as FDS+Evac). You add tdet and ta yourself. The scenario in Part 1 models no pre-movement, so its exit times are travel times only.

A run that stops at its time limit with agents still inside has no RSET, and more seeds do not supply one, because a run that does not finish has no RSET; A crowd in a fire is such a run.

Why not result.evacuation_time?

  • result.evacuation_time is the time at which the simulation loop stopped. The loop stops when no agent is left and no flow source can still spawn, when only incapacitated agents are left, when every mobile agent has stood still for 100 s (deadlock), or at max_simulation_time. An incapacitated agent stays in the simulation, so with one incapacitation evacuation_time is the time the last mobile agent left or, if none remain mobile, the time of the last collapse (#141). It is still not an egress time: read last_exit_time or the trajectory.
  • result.success is False and result.status is "incomplete" when the run reaches max_simulation_time with agents still inside, when the building empties after its flow windows closed with flow agents not spawned, when only incapacitated agents remain inside and no flow window is open (end_reason "all_mobile_left") (#139), or when every mobile agent inside stood still for 100 s (end_reason "deadlock", #760). None of these says when the last mobile agent left. A deadlocked run’s evacuation_time is the time the rule fired, not an egress time and not the time limit. Its stuck agents never left, so count it as a run that did not finish, and do not use its time as a value censored at max_simulation_time.

Part 2 below shows both.

Runnable example

Download the files for this page

↓ Download pyfds-evac-rset-ensemble.zip (22 kB)

The example script, the two scenarios, the FDS deck of part 2, run.py, pinned package versions and a README.txt with the commands and the expected result. FDS output is not included: a clone of the repository has it, or you write it with FDS in about 30 s.

Built from
pyFDS-Evac 5abe7a6; requirements.txt pins the packages of uv.lock
FDS
you run it; the page used FDS-6.10.1-0-g12efa16-release, 30 s wall clock, one process, on an Apple M3 Pro, macOS
pyFDS-Evac run
about 10 s
Expected result
mean = 44.5 s, SD = 1.8 s
min-max = 41.5-46.0 s
95th percentile = 46.0 s
exit times [], incapacitated 1, remaining 1
made at commit 9c820e0f
Licence
decks, scenario files and geometry CC-BY-4.0; code MIT
What is inside (14 files)
  • README.txt: this file
  • LICENSE: MIT licence of the code
  • requirements.txt: pinned Python packages, from uv.lock
  • examples/rset_ensemble.py: the example script
  • run.py: the pyFDS-Evac command line
  • assets/fic_vs_fed_speed/config.json: JuPedSim scenario of part 1
  • assets/fic_vs_fed_speed/geometry.wkt: walkable area of part 1
  • assets/fic_vs_fed_speed/fic_vs_fed_speed.fds: FDS deck of the same corridor; part 1 does not run it
  • assets/fic_vs_fed_speed/build_geometry.py: writes the part 1 deck, scenario and geometry
  • assets/fic_vs_fed_speed/README.md: what the part 1 scenario is
  • assets/iso_table22_coupled/iso_table22_a.fds: FDS deck of the gas room (part 2)
  • assets/iso_table22_coupled/config_a.json: JuPedSim scenario of the gas room
  • assets/iso_table22_coupled/geometry.wkt: walkable area of the gas room
  • assets/iso_table22_coupled/README.md: what the gas room is and where it comes from

README.txt lists the exact versions and the commands. SHA-256: ae837426276e8683f2c8eb94ca69cd3c0d7e9aef44adec04a7b3b03f053977af

The zip holds the decks but no FDS output; its README.txt runs the part 2 deck with FDS first (about 30 s).

The full script is examples/rset_ensemble.py. Run it from the repository root (runtime about 10 s):

uv run python examples/rset_ensemble.py
import json
import pathlib
import sqlite3
import sys
import tempfile

import numpy as np
from matplotlib.figure import Figure

from pyfds_evac import (
 DefaultFedConfig,
 DefaultFedModel,
 FdsFedField,
 TenabilityConfig,
 load_scenario,
 run_scenario,
)

SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
FIGURE = pathlib.Path(
 sys.argv[1]
 if len(sys.argv) > 1
 else pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "egress_exit_curve.png"
)
COLOURS = ["#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#56B4E9"] # Okabe-Ito
LINESTYLES = ["-", "--", "-.", ":", (0, (5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1))]

Read exit times from the trajectory

run_scenario writes the trajectory to a SQLite file (result.sqlite_file) at 10 frames per second. An agent’s exit time is the time of the last frame it appears in, so it is accurate to 0.1 s. Agents still inside at the end appear up to the last frame and are dropped. The incapacitated agents are read from result.fed_history, which exists only when a FED model ran.

def exit_times(result):
 """Exit time [s] of every agent that left, from the trajectory file."""
 con = sqlite3.connect(result.sqlite_file)
 try:
 fps = float(
 con.execute("SELECT value FROM metadata WHERE key = 'fps'").fetchone()[0]
 )
 last = con.execute("SELECT MAX(frame) FROM trajectory_data GROUP BY id")
 times = sorted(frame / fps for (frame,) in last)
 finally:
 con.close()
 # Agents still inside at the end are the ones seen in the last frames.
 return times[: len(times) - result.agents_remaining]


def incapacitated(result):
 """Number of agents incapacitated during the run."""
 rows = result.fed_history or []
 return len({row["agent_id"] for row in rows if row["incapacitated"]})

Part 1: one run per seed

The scenario is assets/fic_vs_fed_speed: 30 agents at one end of a 4 m × 50 m corridor with one exit, in clear air. Each run writes a manifest next to its trajectory, and the loop reads the seed back from it.

scenario = load_scenario("assets/fic_vs_fed_speed")
for name, dist in scenario.distributions.items():
 params = dist["parameters"]
 print(
 f"{name}: {params['number']} agents, "
 f"use_premovement={params.get('use_premovement', False)}"
 )

curves = {}
for seed in SEEDS:
 result = run_scenario(scenario, seed=seed)
 manifest = json.loads(pathlib.Path(result.manifest_file).read_text())
 curves[manifest["seed"]] = exit_times(result)
 print(
 f"seed {manifest['seed']}: last exit {curves[seed][-1]:.1f} s, "
 f"evacuated {len(curves[seed])}, incapacitated {incapacitated(result)}, "
 f"remaining {result.agents_remaining}"
 )
 result.cleanup()
print(f"versions: {manifest['versions']}")
print(f"git: {manifest['git_commit']}, dirty: {manifest['git_dirty']}")

Expected output, without the Evacuated 30/30 … done progress line that run_scenario prints for each run:

jps-distributions_0: 30 agents, use_premovement=False
seed 1: last exit 41.5 s, evacuated 30, incapacitated 0, remaining 0
seed 2: last exit 46.0 s, evacuated 30, incapacitated 0, remaining 0
seed 3: last exit 44.9 s, evacuated 30, incapacitated 0, remaining 0
seed 4: last exit 44.5 s, evacuated 30, incapacitated 0, remaining 0
seed 5: last exit 45.8 s, evacuated 30, incapacitated 0, remaining 0
versions: {'pyfds-evac': '0.1.0', 'jupedsim': '1.4.2', 'fdsreader': '1.11.7', 'fdsvismap': '0.2.1'}
git: b42f07ef4865142d55f3ff9e0e642370f0cb7b56, dirty: True

This loop runs all five seeds in one Python process. Each seed gives the same result as in a process of its own; only the JuPedSim agent ids differ.

The versions and the git state depend on your checkout. dirty: True means the working tree had uncommitted changes when the run started. The seed changes where the agents start in their spawn area, so each seed gives a different time. There is no fire in Part 1, so nobody is incapacitated.

Summarise the last exit over the seeds 

last = np.array([times[-1] for times in curves.values()])
print(f"n = {len(last)} seeds")
print(f"mean = {last.mean():.1f} s, SD = {last.std(ddof=1):.1f} s")
print(f"min-max = {last.min():.1f}-{last.max():.1f} s")
print(f"95th percentile = {np.percentile(last, 95):.1f} s")
n = 5 seeds
mean = 44.5 s, SD = 1.8 s
min-max = 41.5-46.0 s
95th percentile = 46.0 s

Five seeds are too few for a study. They keep this example fast. The SD and the percentiles need many more runs to settle. The 95th percentile uses NumPy’s default linear interpolation; with five values it lies between the two largest. Increase SEEDS, and check that the summary no longer changes much when you add runs. DIN 18009-2:2022-08 recommends at least ten runs of a microscopic model and takes RSET as the 95 % quantile; mean values alone are not suitable (§6.6.2, p. 21; §8.3.1 and Note 2, p. 27).

Plot the exit curves 

fig = Figure(figsize=(6, 4))
ax = fig.subplots()
for (seed, times), colour, style in zip(curves.items(), COLOURS, LINESTYLES):
 counts = np.arange(1, len(times) + 1)
 ax.step(times, counts, where="post", color=colour, ls=style, label=f"seed {seed}")
ax.axvspan(last.min(), last.max(), color="lightgrey", alpha=0.5, lw=0)
ax.text(
 last.min() - 0.3,
 2,
 f"last exit {last.min():.1f}-{last.max():.1f} s\nover {len(last)} seeds",
 color="dimgrey",
 ha="right",
)
ax.grid(color="lightgrey", linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
for spine in ax.spines.values():
 spine.set_visible(False)
ax.tick_params(length=0, labelcolor="dimgrey")
ax.set_xlabel("time since start of simulation [s]", color="dimgrey")
ax.set_ylabel("agents evacuated [-]", color="dimgrey")
ax.legend(
 frameon=True,
 facecolor="white",
 framealpha=0.8,
 edgecolor="lightgrey",
 labelcolor="dimgrey",
)
FIGURE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig(FIGURE, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
print(f"figure: {FIGURE}")

The script writes the figure into a new temporary directory and prints its path. To write it elsewhere, pass the path: uv run python examples/rset_ensemble.py egress_exit_curve.png.

Cumulative number of agents evacuated [-] against time since the start of the simulation [s], assets/fic_vs_fed_speed, N = 30 agents, clear air, no pre-movement. One line per seed, each with its own colour and line style, n = 5 seeds. The grey band spans the last exit time over the seeds, from the earliest to the latest. Exit times are read from the trajectory at 0.1 s resolution. Regenerated by uv run python examples/rset_ensemble.py site/static/images/howto/egress_exit_curve.png.

Part 2: an incapacitated agent and evacuation_time

No tracked FDS case gives incapacitations and exits in the same run within a few seconds of runtime. Part 2 therefore uses the ISO 20414 Test 19 room of the Real-FDS walkthrough: one occupant held still in 0.10 % CO, 2.0 % CO2 and 15.0 % O2, read from the FDS slices in assets/iso_table22_coupled/fds/a.

room = load_scenario("assets/iso_table22_coupled/config_a.json")
gas_dir = "assets/iso_table22_coupled/fds/a"
fed = DefaultFedModel(FdsFedField.from_fds(gas_dir), DefaultFedConfig())
tenability = TenabilityConfig(incapacitation_mode="deterministic")
fire = run_scenario(room, seed=420, fed_model=fed, tenability_config=tenability)
print(
 f"evacuation_time {fire.evacuation_time:.0f} s "
 f"(max_simulation_time {room.max_simulation_time:.0f} s), "
 f"success {fire.success}"
)
print(
 f"exit times {exit_times(fire)}, incapacitated {incapacitated(fire)}, "
 f"remaining {fire.agents_remaining}"
)
fire.cleanup()
evacuation_time 982 s (max_simulation_time 1150 s), success False
exit times [], incapacitated 1, remaining 1

The occupant is incapacitated at 982 s and never leaves. The run ends then, so evacuation_time reports 982 s, and success is False because the run is incomplete. The exit times, the incapacitated count and the remaining count tell you what happened. From the command line, run.py exits with status 2 for such a run (Exit status).

Incapacitation mode

TenabilityConfig() defaults to incapacitation_mode="deterministic": every agent is incapacitated at fed_threshold (1.0), as in FDS+Evac. With TenabilityConfig(incapacitation_mode="probabilistic"), or --incapacitation-mode probabilistic on the command line, each agent draws its own threshold, fed_threshold * exp(susceptibility_sigma * Z) with Z ~ N(0, 1): a log-normal with median fed_threshold. The defaults are on the FED model page. Part 2 uses the deterministic mode.

Related options

  • To add smoke or FED from FDS output to an ensemble, pass the same models to run_scenario inside the loop, as in the Real-FDS walkthrough.
  • To compare RSET from a run without the fire with coupled runs, see Evacuation with and without the fire.
  • Pre-movement is set per spawn area in the scenario JSON, with use_premovement, premovement_distribution (gamma, lognormal, weibull, uniform or constant), premovement_param_a, premovement_param_b and premovement_seed. If premovement_seed is null, it is derived from the run seed, so the pre-movement times change with the seed. If it is set, they stay the same across seeds.
  • Each manifest also records uv_lock_sha256, scenario_path, fds_dir, fds_version and created_utc. cleanup() deletes it with the trajectory, so copy both first if you want to keep them. With run.py --output-sqlite PATH, the manifest is copied next to PATH as <stem>.manifest.json.

See also

  • Quickstart
  • Real-FDS walkthrough

item.title: How do I check each agent against ASET with FED, as in Pathfinder?
item.description:
A Pathfinder-style check keeps the occupants moving through the fire’s smoke, records the dose each one collects on the way, and compares the time a limit is reached with the time the occupant leaves. This page does the same with --output-fed-summary. It reads no new physics: the summary is a post-processing of the FED and smoke histories the run already writes.

You need the FDS output of A crowd in a fire in $FDS. Nothing here runs FDS.

1. Keep the occupants walking and the dose on

--disable-tenability turns off the irritant slowdown and both incapacitation checks. Smoke still slows walking, and the gas FED, the heat FED and the FIC are still accumulated and written. Nobody drops, so every agent has one RSET and the margin to each limit is defined for all of them.

uv run python run.py --scenario assets/t_junction --fds-dir "$FDS" \
 --disable-tenability \
 --output-fed-summary tj/summary.csv

This checks a design: the occupants are not allowed to fall. Leaving the checks on, and the dose with them, answers a different question, what happens to the people once they drop. Run both when both matter.

2. Read the summary

One row per agent. For each criterion there are three columns:

  • t_<criterion>_s: first sample time at which the value reached the threshold (>=), empty if never;
  • diff_<criterion>_s: crossing time minus exit time, so a negative value means the limit was reached before the agent left (the sign of DIFF = ASET - RSET);
  • outcome_<criterion>: fail, pass, open or not_evaluated.

An agent still inside at max_simulation_time has no exit time (censored is True, exit_time_s is empty). If it crossed, it failed, with no margin. If it did not, the outcome is open: its margin is undetermined, and the summary never fills it from the last frame. Read the counts of pass only together with the number of censored agents.

Heat is not_evaluated when the run had no TEMPERATURE slice, not ambient. The run’s console output ends with one line per criterion giving the outcome counts and the first crossing.

The thresholds are options: --summary-fed-low and --summary-fed-high (0.3 and 1) for the gas FED, the heat FED and the FIC; --summary-visibility-limit-m (10 m) and --summary-visibility-c (3) for the visibility, which is crossed when K reaches C / limit, 0.3 1/m by default. See Outputs for the columns and the sources of the defaults.

What differs from Pathfinder

These are differences in the run, not in the summary:

  • the O2 term starts below 20 % here and below 19.5 % in Pathfinder (set --o2-threshold-percent 19.5 to match);
  • the speed in smoke follows Lund by default here; Fridolf’s Eq. 7 is available and is being verified (#146);
  • the gas is read at one slice height for everyone, not at each occupant’s own height (#150, #157).

The crossing time has the resolution of --smoke-update-interval (1 s by default). An agent that crossed between its last sample and its exit reads pass.
